newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian hijacker flees after releasing hostages.
newsitem.headline: Russian hijacker flees after releasing hostages.

text.p: A man armed with a grenade held dozens of people hostage for over an hour on a bus in southern Russia on Monday before releasing most of them and fleeing with a captive local politician, news agencies said.

Interfax news agency quoted interior ministry officials in the North Caucasus region of Dagestan, as saying the lone hijacker later released the politician, who had offered himself in exchange for the passengers, and three other hostages before crossed into neighbouring Chechnya on foot.
Itar-Tass news agency, citing a source in one of Russia's "power ministries" said there were conflicting versions of where the hijacker had gone.
According to one, he had crossed into Chechnya, by another he was in hiding in Dagestan, which neighbours Chechnya.
Tass had earlier said there were two hijackers.
A spokesman for the interior ministry in Moscow initially said two or three hijackers seized the bus with 35 people aboard
But chief Russian interior ministry spokesman Alexander Furs was quoted by ORT state television as saying there was only one hijacker and 48 people on the bus.
The incident began in the Dagestan capital Makhachkala around 6.30 p.m. (1430 GMT).
Police in Dagestan, scene of a bloody hostage-taking by Chechen separatist guerrillas in January, said they were sure the unidentified man or men involved were Chechen.
The hostages were all released after negotiations by a member of Dagestan's regional assembly, Gadzhi Makhachev.
The hijacker at first had demanded a helicopter and took the bus to the airport, the interior ministry spokesman said.
But Makhachev took the man off in the politician's own Lada saloon.

Police said they were blocking roads but apparently did not prevent the car reaching the Dagestan town of Khasavyurt, 100 km (60 miles) from the Caspian Sea port of Makhachkala, on the Dagestan-Chechnya frontier.
Interfax said the man released Makhachev and the three remaining hostages near Khasavyurt around 9 p.m. and walked over into Chechnya.
Early reports of the incident stirred memories from last January, when Chechen guerrillas led by Salman Raduyev took hundreds of hostages in the Dagestan town of Kizlyar.
They then withstood days of Russian air and artillery bombardment in the village of Pervomaiskoye, near Khasavyurt, before escaping back across the Chechen border.

However, later details suggested the incident may have been either unplanned or a non-political criminal hold-up, reminiscent of several bus hijackings in the North Caucasus in recent years, often by Chechens.
On September 20, 1995, two hijackers demanded $1.5 million and a helicopter after seizing a bus in Makhachkala. The next day police stormed the vehicle, arresting the men and freeing all 18 hostages.

In May 1994, four Chechens were arrested after hijacking a school bus near Vladikavkaz and flying four of the hostages by helicopter with them back to Chechnya. A month later, three gunmen were captured as they tried to flee with their ransom after holding a busload of passengers near Mineralniye Vody.
In December 1993, police arrested four men in Makhachkala, freeing teenagers seized at a school in the southern Russian city of Rostov and flown by helicopter across the region.
